task_title: rust-bam with view, flagstat, idxstats, quickcheck, index, sort
status_statement: The crate is implemented on noodles 0.118.0 and the samtools 1.24 differential was RUN: 20/20 cases pass. The MSRV decision was resolved explicitly and is testable in both directions. Nothing here is a second-hand claim.
previous_blocker: noodles 0.118.0 was absent from the offline Cargo registry; now resolved at the dependency level.

acceptance_matrix.criterion: rust-bam crate with all six subcommands
SAM text identical to samtools view
BAM header+records identical after samtools view -h

acceptance_matrix.detail: samtools quickcheck exit 0; byte-reproducible across runs
BAI byte-identical; htslib answers region queries via our index
639 tests; cutadapt, UMI-tools, W1-3 and M3 all green

dependency.plan_decision: D2 - noodles for new SAM/BAM work, to avoid the C toolchain and htslib CVE surface
dependency.note_on_features: There is no `bgzipped` feature; the first probe used it and cargo rejected it. Valid features were read from the crate metadata.

msrv_decision.required_by: noodles 0.118.0 and every sub-crate declare rust-version = 1.91.0
msrv_decision.declared_in: [workspace.package] rust-version in the root Cargo.toml, with the reasoning inline
msrv_decision.why_not_silent: Leaving 1.88 while rust-bam depends on noodles would be a claim cargo cannot honour; the workspace would simply refuse to build.
consequences: The other five crates are buildable on 1.88 today, but a shared workspace declares one floor, so their effective minimum rises to 1.91.
A separate workspace for rust-bam was rejected because W1-1 established one workspace for all crates.

verified_both_directions.on_1_88_0: rustup run 1.88.0 cargo build --offline -p rust-bam -> error: noodles@0.118.0 requires rustc 1.91.0

normalisation_rules.name: pg_lines
normalisation_rules.what: drops @PG lines from BOTH sides before comparison
normalisation_rules.why_required: samtools appends its own @PG line recording its version and command line; it names the tool, so it can never match between two implementations, and it carries no alignment content
normalisation_rules.evidence: diff of view -h before the rule was exactly one line: '@PG ID:samtools.1 PN:samtools PP:samtools VN:1.24 CL:samtools view -h basic.bam'
normalisation_rules.what_is_still_compared: @HD, @SQ, @RG and any input-originated @PG line, byte for byte
normalisation_rules.self_test_guards: the rule must neither under-match nor over-match; '@PGx\tnot a header' must survive

bgzf_and_bam.eof_marker_note: The 28-byte marker with gzip XFL = 0 is pinned as BGZF_EOF_MARKER in commands.rs and asserted by a unit test — the exact byte W1-4 previously found wrong in bioinfo-fastx.
bgzf_and_bam.byte_identical_justification: BGZF block boundaries are an encoding choice, not part of the format contract; decoded content and container validity are what match.

index_interoperability.evidence: samtools view -c sorted.bam chr1 answered 8 via our .bai, matching the count using samtools' own index

order: reference sequence id in @SQ header order
forward strand before reverse at the same position
original input index (makes the order total)
sort_order.steps_5_to_6_are_additions: samtools leaves such ties unspecified; adding them makes output reproducible, which the plan requires
sort_order.stable_verified: sort_ties passes and repeated runs are byte-identical

bugs_found_and_fixed.confirmation: an isolated 2-record fixture showed flag 0x1 alone is counted, and 0x8 (mate unmapped) must exclude
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: stats::FlagStat::add keys on 0x1 and not-0x8, no 0x2 requirement

bugs_found_and_fixed.bug: -h collided with clap's auto help short flag and panicked at CLI build time
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: disable_help_flag(true) on view, explicit --help that does not require <FILE>

bugs_found_and_fixed.bug: malformed input exited 3 where samtools exits 1
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: unparseable/corrupt input is ExitClass::Runtime (1); 3 reserved for actionable preconditions like indexing an unsorted BAM

bugs_found_and_fixed.bug: 4 bytes consumed by the magic sniff were not handed back to the gzip decoder
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: re-prepend the consumed prefix with Cursor::chain

bugs_found_and_fixed.bug: compared a Position to a usize

fixture_bugs_found_and_fixed: The first BASIC_SAM was not coordinate-sorted, so samtools itself refused to index it ('Chromosome blocks not continuous'); reordered.
A headerless SAM cannot be converted to BAM ('no SQ lines present in the header'); that case now exercises SAM input directly.

harness_defects_fixed.defect: build_fixtures must create its own per-case work directory
harness_defects_fixed.why: this is the exact bug that crashed the W1-3 harness before case 1

harness_defects_fixed.defect: tool paths must be absolute because every case runs with cwd=<work>
harness_defects_fixed.guard: os.path.abspath on the rust binary; samtools resolved to an absolute path

harness_defects_fixed.defect: the first @PG regex left a blank line behind, which would itself be a spurious difference

negative_controls.conclusion: the differential detects a one-character formatting regression

suites.name: MSRV 1.88.0 refusal
suites.result: refused, naming noodles 1.91.0 as the requirement (as intended)

limitations: CRAM is not supported: detected and rejected with a clear message rather than misparsed
CSI indexes are not written; only BAI (samtools index -c is unmatched)
rust-bam view has no region argument (chr1:100-200); htslib can use our index, but we do not consume it ourselves
sort buffers the whole file in memory; memory is proportional to input size, not bounded
no -t/--threads, -f/-F/-q filters, -L BED input, or -s sampling
byte-identical BAM to samtools is not claimed and is not achievable, because BGZF block boundaries legitimately differ
samtools' tie order for records identical in name and position is unspecified; rust-bam adds name then input index to make the order total (DR-W1-4-3)
not_claimed: region queries on our own side
